answer: No. Your records show lisinopril was stopped on September 22, 2025, because it caused a dry cough, and you were switched to losartan 50 mg once a day. Please do not restart lisinopril unless your doctor tells you to. The app is most likely showing an old copy of your medication list from before that change. Your pharmacy record does not list lisinopril either. Please ask Dr. Marsh's office to confirm your current list, and ask for the cough to be recorded as a lisinopril intolerance, because several of your records list only aspirin as an allergy.
short: Lisinopril was stopped September 22, 2025 for dry cough and replaced by losartan. Please confirm the current list with Dr. Marsh and correct the app.

knowledge.says: Cough is a known side effect of ACE inhibitors such as lisinopril. Losartan belongs to a different class (an ARB) that rarely causes cough, which is why it was chosen as the replacement.
knowledge.guideline: Common practice: switch from an ACE inhibitor to an ARB when ACE-inhibitor cough occurs, and record the intolerance.
